title: Lesson 4: Contact, Feeling, Craving, Clinging — The Ignite Switch of Samsara

suttaRef.title: The Great Causes Discourse (Mahānidāna Sutta — DN 15)
suttaRef.excerptPali: 'Vedanāpaccayā taṇhā'ti iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ... Taṇhāpaccayā pariyesanā, pariyesanāpaccayā lābho, lābhapaccayā vinicchayo, vinicchayapaccayā chandarāgo... Etampeso, ānanda, pariyāyo yena vedanāpaccayā taṇhā veditabbā.
suttaRef.excerptTranslation: 'With feeling as condition, craving comes to be': thus it has been said... Craving conditions pursuit; pursuit conditions gain; gain conditions decision-making; decision-making conditions desire and lust; desire and lust condition clinging; clinging conditions possessiveness; possessiveness conditions stinginess; stinginess conditions safeguarding; and conditioned by safeguarding, many bad unwholesome things arise: taking up of sticks and knives, conflicts, quarrels, insults, and falsehoods!

pariyatti.shortSummary: The Mahānidāna Sutta (DN 15) exposes the socio-psychological engine of wars, conflicts, and family betrayals: all ignite from bare feeling (*Vedanā*) sparking Craving (*Taṇhā*), mutating into Clinging (*Upādāna*), possessiveness, safeguarding, and violent warfare.

coreConcepts.definition: The confluence of sense organ, sense object, and corresponding consciousness.
Unquenchable thirst for sensual gratification (*Kāmataṇhā*), becoming (*Bhavataṇhā*), or non-becoming (*Vibhavataṇhā*).
Fierce possessive grasping: sensual clinging, dogma clinging, ritual clinging, and ego clinging.

pariyatti.expositionMarkdown:
### 1. The Anatomy of Global Conflict
Pleasant sensation sparks Craving ➔ Pursuit ➔ Acquisition ➔ Greed ➔ Possessiveness ➔ Jealousy ➔ Weaponized defense ➔ Global warfare! The Buddha traced all geopolitical slaughter to unexamined pleasant feeling.

### 2. Flipping the Circuit Breaker
You cannot gouge your eyes out to avoid contact. But **you can cut the circuit at Feeling before it sparks Craving.** Enjoy the meal with clear comprehension without becoming an addicted slave to taste!

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Blaming Feeling (*Vedanā*) as the evil villain.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Feeling is innocent neurobiology. The criminal culprit is Craving (*Taṇhā*) latching onto it.

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Non-clinging means abandoning family responsibilities and becoming cold.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Non-clinging liberates you from possessive neurosis, empowering you to love and serve with pure, unselfish wisdom.

patipatti.practiceGuide:
1. 3-Second Purchasing Pause: When seduced by a consumer product, pause 3 seconds and ask: 'Is this real utility or eye-craving?'.
2. Mindful Eating: Observe craving before tasting; taste attentively; watch taste disappear down the throat.
patipatti.suggestedVirtue: Mastery over sensory thirst, preserving uncompromised inner sovereignty.

pativedha.reflectionPrompt: Did you taste the majestic freedom of admiring something alluring without the slightest impulse to possess it?
selfAuditChecklist: I intercepted at least one impulsive wave of unnecessary craving.
I refrained from treating relationships as possessive ownership.
My mind felt spacious and uncluttered by consumerist compulsions.
